data.q: Which instrument is the principal current Indian statute in the hierarchy described in this chapter?
data.e: Bharatiya Vayuyan Adhiniyam 2024 is the principal current Indian statute, while the Rules and Civil Aviation Requirements provide more detailed requirements.

data.q: Which Indian authority has the core civil aviation security oversight role?
data.e: BCAS is the authority responsible for civil aviation security policy, standards and oversight.

data.q: Which definition describes a non-power driven heavier than air aircraft deriving lift chiefly from fixed surfaces?
data.e: Glider is the correct term for a non-power driven heavier than air aircraft that derives lift chiefly from fixed surfaces.

data.q: Which operation is neither commercial air transport nor aerial work?
data.e: General aviation is defined as an aircraft operation other than commercial air transport or aerial work.

data.q: When a pressure altimeter is set to QNH, which vertical quantity does it indicate?
data.e: Altitude is indicated with QNH because altitude is referenced to mean sea level.

data.q: Which minimum provides at least 1,000 ft obstacle clearance within a 25 NM sector centred on a radio navigation aid?
data.e: MSA is the minimum sector altitude, providing at least 1,000 ft clearance within a 25 NM sector.

data.q: Which airspace begins at the surface and extends upward to a specified upper limit?
data.e: A control zone is controlled airspace extending upwards from the surface to a specified upper limit.

data.q: Which navigation specification includes on-board performance monitoring and alerting?
data.e: An RNP specification includes the requirement for on-board performance monitoring and alerting.

data.q: Which aerodrome area consists of the manoeuvring area plus the apron or aprons?
data.e: The movement area consists of the manoeuvring area and the apron or aprons.

data.q: Which declared distance equals TORA plus stopway, if a stopway is provided?
data.e: ASDA is the accelerate-stop distance available and equals TORA plus the stopway, if provided.

data.q: Which flight plan includes changes resulting from subsequent clearances?
data.e: The current flight plan is the flight plan including changes brought about by later clearances.

data.q: Which emergency phase means reasonable certainty that grave and imminent danger exists and immediate assistance is required?
data.e: DETRESFA is the distress phase, used when grave and imminent danger is reasonably certain and immediate assistance is required.

data.q: Which Chicago Convention Article establishes complete and exclusive State sovereignty over the airspace above its territory?
data.e: Article 1 establishes complete and exclusive sovereignty over the airspace above a State's territory.

data.q: What does Article 6 require before a scheduled international air service operates over or into another State?
o: Special permission or authorisation from that State
data.e: Special permission or authorisation from that State is required for a scheduled international air service under Article 6.

data.q: Which item is one of the seven documents listed under Article 29?
o: Passenger health card for every flight
data.e: A certificate of registration is one of the documents Article 29 requires an aircraft in international navigation to carry.

data.q: Within what period does Article 38 require notice after an amended international Standard when a State does not amend its own practice?
data.e: The required period stated by Article 38 is 60 days after adoption of the amendment.

data.q: Which ICAO body has all Contracting States represented with one vote each?
data.e: The Assembly includes all Contracting States, with one vote for each State.

data.q: Which body adopts international Standards and Recommended Practices?
data.e: The Council adopts international Standards and Recommended Practices, while technical bodies prepare and recommend material.

data.q: Which Annex addresses safe transport of dangerous goods by air?
data.e: Annex 18 addresses the safe transport of dangerous goods by air.

data.q: What status do Regional Supplementary Procedures have?
o: They are national laws in every State
They are Council-approved procedures for the relevant region
They apply only to military aircraft
data.e: Regional Supplementary Procedures are approved by the Council and apply only in the relevant region.

data.q: Which freedom permits landing in another State for refuelling without taking on or putting down traffic?
data.e: The second freedom permits a non-traffic technical landing such as refuelling or repair.

data.q: Which convention chiefly addresses unlawful seizure of aircraft?
data.e: The Hague Convention 1970 chiefly addresses suppression of unlawful seizure of aircraft.

data.q: Which convention concerns damage caused by foreign aircraft to persons or property on the surface?
data.e: The Rome Convention 1952 concerns liability for damage caused by foreign aircraft to third parties on the surface.

data.q: Which Indian body is responsible for civil aviation safety regulation, licensing and airworthiness oversight?
data.e: DGCA is the Indian safety regulator responsible for licensing, airworthiness and related oversight.

data.q: Which law replaced the Aircraft Act, 1934 as India's principal civil aviation enabling statute?
data.e: The Bharatiya Vayuyan Adhiniyam, 2024 replaced the Aircraft Act, 1934 as the principal enabling statute.

data.q: Which body has the central role of investigating aircraft accidents and incidents in India?
data.e: The Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau is the body responsible for investigating aircraft accidents and incidents.

data.q: What must an Indian registered aircraft normally obtain before leaving India for an overseas flight?
data.e: Required DGCA permission is needed before an Indian registered aircraft leaves India for an overseas flight.

data.q: If a pilot strays into a prohibited area under the rule summarised by Bali, what is the correct immediate course?
o: Circle until a clearance is received
Signal distress, leave the area and land at the nearest aerodrome
data.e: The stated response is to signal distress, leave the prohibited area and land at the nearest aerodrome.

data.q: How long before flight does Bali state that flight crew must avoid alcohol, sedatives and narcotics?
data.e: Bali states a 12-hour prohibition before flight, together with the continuing rule against operating while intoxicated.

data.q: At what jet-exhaust distance does the fuelling rule in the lesson require fuelling to stop?
data.e: Fuelling stops when hazardous jet exhaust comes within 43 m of the fuelling equipment or aircraft.

data.q: For how long must a flight crew log book be preserved under the stated rule?
o: At least five years after the last entry
Two years after the first entry
data.e: The personal flight crew log book is retained for at least five years after its last entry.

data.q: For how long is a draft CAR placed on the DGCA website for objections and suggestions before final issue?
data.e: The stated consultation period for a draft CAR is 30 days before final issue.

data.q: Which publication is used for urgent, time-sensitive information about a facility, service, procedure or hazard?
data.e: A NOTAM provides time-sensitive operational information whose timely knowledge is essential.

data.q: Which airspace type permits flight only in accordance with specified conditions?
data.e: A restricted area permits flight only in accordance with its specified conditions.

data.q: What identifier is assigned to a registered drone under the Drone Rules system?
data.e: A registered drone receives a Unique Identification Number, commonly shortened to UIN.

data.q: What general maximum fine is stated in Bali's summary of the 2024 Act?
data.e: Bali's summary states a general maximum fine of Rs. 1 crore, alongside imprisonment up to two years or both.

data.q: Which ICAO Annex contains the Standards for aircraft nationality and registration marks?
data.e: Annex 7 contains the international Standards for Aircraft Nationality and Registration Marks.

data.q: Who assigns the individual registration mark to an aircraft?
o: The State of Registry or common mark registering authority
data.e: The State of Registry or common mark registering authority assigns the aircraft's registration mark.

data.q: Which combination must be excluded because it can be confused with an urgency signal?
data.e: PAN is an internationally recognised urgency signal and must not be used as a registration-mark combination.

data.q: Which mark does Bali identify for Indian civil aircraft?
data.e: VT is the nationality mark that Bali identifies as continuing in use for Indian civil aircraft.

data.q: What is the minimum height of marks on the wings of a heavier-than-air aircraft?
data.e: The wing marks of a heavier-than-air aircraft must be at least 50 cm high.

data.q: Where are the wing marks placed on a heavier-than-air aircraft?
o: Only on the upper wing surface
data.e: The required wing marks are placed on the lower wing surface for ready external identification.

data.q: What minimum height applies to marks on the fuselage or vertical tail of a heavier-than-air aircraft?
data.e: Fuselage and vertical-tail marks on a heavier-than-air aircraft must be at least 30 cm high.

data.q: Which document is evidence that an aircraft has been entered on the national register?
data.e: The Certificate of Registration is the official evidence that the aircraft has been entered on the national register.

data.q: Which item is specifically added to the Indian Certificate of Registration for a leased aircraft?
o: Lease validity and particulars of lessor and lessee
Every airport in the intended route network
data.e: A leased aircraft's certificate includes the lease validity and the names, nationalities and addresses of lessor and lessee.

data.q: Which event is a stated ground for DGCA cancellation of Indian registration?
o: A routine change of parking stand
The Certificate of Airworthiness has been expired for five years or more
Replacement of a cabin seat cover
data.e: A Certificate of Airworthiness that has remained expired for five years or more is a stated cancellation ground.

data.q: Who exercises operational control over a leased aircraft in Bali's summary?
data.e: The lessee operator exercises operational control and must hold the necessary economic and operating authority.

data.q: What does a common mark replace for a qualifying international operating agency?
data.e: A common mark replaces the nationality mark for a qualifying international operating agency.

data.q: Which ICAO Annex contains the international airworthiness Standards?
data.e: Annex 8 contains the international Standards for the airworthiness of aircraft.

data.q: Which State determines whether an aircraft on its register continues to be airworthy?
data.e: The State of Registry determines whether an aircraft on its register continues to be airworthy.

data.q: What is the main purpose of a Type Certificate?
data.e: A Type Certificate records approval of the type design after compliance with the applicable design requirements is shown.

data.q: Which document summarises approved models, certification basis, powerplant combinations and design limitations?
data.e: The Type Certificate Data Sheet summarises the approved design data and limitations associated with the Type Certificate.

data.q: What must be true before DGCA issues a normal Certificate of Airworthiness?
o: The aircraft must have flown internationally
The owner must also be the manufacturer
The aircraft must conform to its approved design and be safe to operate
The Noise Certificate must replace the flight manual
data.e: DGCA issues the normal Certificate of Airworthiness only when the aircraft conforms to its approved basis and is in a condition for safe operation.

data.q: What does an Airworthiness Review Certificate record?
o: Approval of a new aircraft type
Permission to use a radio frequency
data.e: An Airworthiness Review Certificate records that the required periodic continuing-airworthiness review was completed satisfactorily.

data.q: Which action belongs to continuing airworthiness?
o: Controlling defects and complying with mandatory airworthiness instructions
Changing the nationality mark without approval
Ignoring an applicable directive until the next sale
Replacing technical records with the journey log
data.e: Controlling defects and complying with mandatory airworthiness instructions are core continuing-airworthiness duties.

data.q: Who ensures a structural integrity programme, including corrosion-control information, exists for the applicable type?
data.e: The State of Design ensures that the applicable structural integrity programme includes corrosion-control information.

data.q: Which event causes the certificate to be deemed suspended under Bali's national provisions?
data.e: Major damage is one of the events that causes the Certificate of Airworthiness to be deemed suspended.

data.q: What may the Director General require when there is reasonable doubt about aircraft safety?
o: A change of aircraft nationality only
Inspection, repair, replacement, overhaul or flight testing under approved supervision
data.e: The Director General may require inspection, repair, replacement, overhaul or flight testing under approved supervision.

data.q: What does a special flight permit authorise?
o: Any flight selected by the pilot
A specific exceptional flight subject to stated limitations
Permanent restoration of the normal certificate
data.e: A special flight permit authorises a specific exceptional flight subject to its stated purpose and limitations.

data.q: Which document answers whether the aircraft meets an applicable certified noise standard?
data.e: The Noise Certificate records compliance of the approved aircraft configuration with the applicable certified noise standard.

data.q: What is the minimum age stated by Bali for an aeroplane CPL?
data.e: The minimum age for an aeroplane Commercial Pilot's Licence is 18 years.

data.q: Which language level is Operational and must be re-evaluated every three years?
data.e: Level 4 is Operational, is accepted, and requires re-evaluation every three years.

data.q: What is the normal Class 2 medical validity up to age 50?
data.e: The normal Class 2 medical validity is two years up to age 50.

data.q: Which restriction applies to an SPL holder?
o: The holder may carry one passenger
The holder may fly for hire under supervision
The holder may fly IFR after ten solo hours
The holder flies under VFR and may not carry passengers
data.e: An SPL holder flies under VFR and may not carry passengers, animals or goods.

data.q: What total flight experience does Bali state for the aeroplane PPL?
data.e: The aeroplane PPL requires at least 40 hours of total flight time.

data.q: What recent night experience is required before a PPL holder carries passengers at night?
o: Five take-offs and five landings by night as pilot-in-command in six months
Ten night landings in twelve months
Five instrument approaches in six months
data.e: The PPL holder needs five take-offs and five landings by night as pilot-in-command within the preceding six months.

data.q: Which set correctly states the CPL core experience?
data.e: The CPL core is 200 total hours, 100 hours as pilot-in-command and 20 hours cross-country as pilot-in-command.

data.q: How long is the type proficiency check described for transport aeroplanes above 5,700 kg valid?
data.e: The applicable type proficiency check is valid for six months.

data.q: What total time does Bali state for the aeroplane ATPL?
data.e: The aeroplane ATPL requires at least 1,500 hours of total flight time.

data.q: What is the ATPL minimum total night-flight experience?
data.e: The ATPL experience table requires at least 75 hours of night flight.

data.q: What is the normal validity of an aeroplane Instrument Rating from its flight test?
data.e: The aeroplane Instrument Rating is valid for twelve months from the instrument flight test.

data.q: Which time must the student log as SPIC with the instructor named in remarks?
data.e: Student pilot-in-command time is logged by the student as SPIC with the instructor named in the remarks.

data.q: When may the pilot-in-command depart from a Rule of the Air?
o: Only when absolutely necessary in the interests of safety
data.e: A pilot-in-command may depart from a Rule only when circumstances make it absolutely necessary in the interests of safety.

data.q: What must pre-flight action include for an IFR flight?
o: Current weather, fuel requirements and an alternative course of action
data.e: IFR pre-flight action includes current weather information, fuel requirements and an alternative course of action if the plan cannot be completed.

data.q: What is the VFR minimum over a congested area when no exception applies?
o: 1,000 ft above the highest obstacle within 600 m
2,000 ft above every obstacle within 8 km
data.e: The VFR congested-area minimum is 1,000 ft above the highest obstacle within 600 m.

data.q: What does Bali state about civil formation flight in India?
o: It is freely permitted below 3,000 ft
It is mandatory for training aircraft
data.e: Bali states that civil formation flight is not permitted in India.

data.q: In a converging encounter at the same level, which aircraft gives way?
o: The aircraft with the other on its left
The aircraft with the other on its right
The larger aircraft in every case
data.e: The aircraft that has the other aircraft on its right gives way.

data.q: What action is required in an approximately head-on encounter?
o: Both aircraft alter heading to the right
data.e: In a head-on or approximately head-on encounter, both aircraft alter heading to the right.

data.q: Who has right-of-way during overtaking?
o: The aircraft on the right only
data.e: The aircraft being overtaken has right-of-way, and the overtaking aircraft keeps clear by altering to the right.

data.q: When may an aircraft cross a lighted stop bar?
o: Only after the lights are switched off and the required clearance exists
Whenever the pilot has received a taxi route
data.e: An aircraft proceeds beyond a stop bar only after the lights are switched off and the required clearance exists.

data.q: Which navigation light is displayed on the aircraft's port side?
data.e: The port navigation light is red.

data.q: For an Indian semicircular track of 225 degrees, which IFR family normally applies below the RVSM transition?
o: Any level selected by the pilot
data.e: A track from 180 through 359 degrees uses the even-thousand IFR family.

data.q: What does a VI R designator identify?
data.e: VI R identifies an Indian restricted area, which may be entered only under the published conditions.

data.q: Which maximum vertical displacement from the leader is stated for an authorised formation?
data.e: The Annex 2 formation condition limits vertical displacement from the leader to 30 m or 100 ft.

chapter: Rules of the Air: VFR, IFR and Signals

data.q: What flight visibility is required at or above 10,000 ft AMSL under the standard VMC table?
data.e: The standard VMC minimum at or above 10,000 ft AMSL is 8 km flight visibility.

chapter: Rules of the Air: VFR, IFR and Signals

data.q: Which statement describes a Special VFR flight?
o: It may ignore ATC in a control zone
It is an IFR flight in visual conditions
It is individually cleared within a control zone and remains clear of cloud with the surface in sight
It is available above FL 150 without approval
data.e: Special VFR is an individually cleared control-zone operation that remains clear of cloud and in sight of the surface.

chapter: Rules of the Air: VFR, IFR and Signals

data.q: Which flight always requires a flight plan under the listed rules?
o: A flight crossing an international border
data.e: A flight crossing an international border is one of the flights for which a flight plan is required.

chapter: Rules of the Air: VFR, IFR and Signals

data.q: What is the general IFR obstacle margin over high or mountainous terrain?
o: 2,000 ft above the highest obstacle within 8 km
data.e: Over high or mountainous terrain, the general IFR minimum is 2,000 ft above the highest obstacle within 8 km.

chapter: Rules of the Air: VFR, IFR and Signals

data.q: Which radiotelephony word indicates an urgency condition?
data.e: PAN PAN is the radiotelephony urgency signal.

chapter: Rules of the Air: VFR, IFR and Signals

data.q: What is the first visual response to the interceptor's follow-me signal?
o: Rock the wings, flash navigation lights and follow
Make an abrupt 90 degree turn away
data.e: The intercepted aircraft acknowledges the follow-me signal by rocking its wings, flashing navigation lights and following.

chapter: Rules of the Air: VFR, IFR and Signals

data.q: What do red flashes from the tower mean to an aircraft in flight?
data.e: Red flashes to an aircraft in flight mean the aerodrome is unsafe and the aircraft must not land.

chapter: Rules of the Air: VFR, IFR and Signals

data.q: Which marshalling signal calls for an emergency stop?
o: Abruptly crossing the raised wands above the head
Holding both arms at 45 degrees downward
data.e: An emergency stop is signalled by abruptly raising and crossing the wands above the head.

chapter: Rules of the Air: VFR, IFR and Signals

data.q: What does a white dumbbell in the signal area mean?
o: Landing, take-off and taxiing are confined to runways and taxiways
data.e: A white dumbbell means landing, take-off and taxiing are confined to runways and taxiways.

chapter: Rules of the Air: VFR, IFR and Signals

data.q: After an IFR flight encounters visual conditions, when is IFR cancelled?
o: When ATC first sees the aircraft
Only after the pilot explicitly cancels IFR and reports the plan change
data.e: Visual conditions do not cancel IFR automatically; the pilot must explicitly cancel IFR and communicate the flight-plan change.

chapter: Rules of the Air: VFR, IFR and Signals

data.q: What sustained true-airspeed deviation is reported under Bali's flight-plan change rule?
data.e: A sustained deviation of Mach 0.02 or 10 kt from the filed true airspeed is reported.

chapter: Rules of the Air: VFR, IFR and Signals

data.q: Which navigation-light combination shows another aircraft approaching approximately head-on?
data.e: Seeing both red and green navigation lights indicates an approaching, approximately head-on aspect.

data.q: Which ATS objective is served by notifying rescue organisations about an aircraft needing aid?
o: The search and rescue support objective
data.e: Notifying and assisting the organisations responsible for search and rescue is one of the five ATS objectives.

data.q: Which airspace structure begins at the surface and protects arriving and departing controlled flights?
data.e: A control zone begins at the surface and contains the relevant arriving and departing flight paths.

data.q: In which class are IFR and VFR admitted and all aircraft separated from each other?
data.e: Class B admits IFR and VFR and provides separation between every aircraft.

data.q: Which second letter belongs to the Chennai FIR family in an Indian location indicator?
data.e: The Chennai FIR family uses O as the second letter, as in VOMM.

data.q: What does prefix U indicate in an ATS route designator?
o: A route or portion in upper airspace
data.e: Prefix U identifies an ATS route or portion established in upper airspace.

data.q: Which item must be read back when transmitted by voice?
data.e: An ATC route clearance is safety-related information that must always be read back when transmitted by voice.

data.q: Where may Voice ATIS never be transmitted?
o: On the voice channel of an ILS
On a suitable VOR voice channel
data.e: Voice ATIS must not be transmitted on the ILS voice channel.

data.q: Which condition can directly trigger ALERFA?
o: Failure to land within five minutes after landing clearance with communication not restored
A normal change of cruise level
Arrival exactly on the estimated time
data.e: Failure to land within five minutes after landing clearance, combined with loss of communication, is an ALERFA trigger.

data.q: What is the minimum stated lower limit of a control area?
o: 200 m or 700 ft above ground or water
data.e: Bali states that the lower limit of a control area must be at least 200 m or 700 ft above ground or water.

data.q: What service is given to participating IFR flights in Class F airspace?
o: Air traffic advisory service plus flight information
data.e: Participating IFR flights in Class F receive air traffic advisory service and flight information.

data.q: What is the RVSM vertical band stated in the lesson?
data.e: RVSM airspace extends from FL 290 through FL 410 inclusive.

data.q: What is essential traffic?
o: Any VFR aircraft parked on an apron
Controlled traffic to which separation applies but the required minimum is not or will not be maintained
data.e: Essential traffic is controlled traffic to which separation should apply but which is not, or will not be, separated by the required minimum.

data.q: What is the normal vertical separation minimum below FL 290?
data.e: Below FL 290, the normal vertical separation minimum is 1,000 ft.

data.q: When does the Bali VOR divergence method establish lateral separation?
o: At 5 degrees with both aircraft overhead
At 30 degrees with no distance condition
At 15 degrees with at least one aircraft 15 NM from the facility
data.e: The VOR method uses at least 15 degrees divergence with one aircraft at least 15 NM from the facility.

data.q: Which angular difference is classified as reciprocal track?
data.e: A reciprocal-track relationship is more than 135 degrees but less than 225 degrees, so 180 degrees qualifies.

data.q: What time minimum may be used when the leader is at least 40 kt faster and the stated same-track conditions are met?
data.e: The same-track same-level minimum may reduce to 3 minutes when the leader is at least 40 kt faster and all stated geometry conditions are met.

data.q: What is the basic DME or GNSS distance minimum for aircraft at the same level on the same track?
data.e: The basic common-reference DME or GNSS minimum for same-level same-track aircraft is 20 NM.

data.q: Which technique requires turbojet aircraft to maintain an ATC-assigned speed expressed as Mach number?
data.e: Mach number technique uses assigned Mach numbers to stabilise relative speed and preserve longitudinal spacing.

data.q: What surveillance wake minimum applies to a Light aircraft following a Heavy aircraft?
data.e: A Light aircraft following a Heavy aircraft requires 6 NM surveillance wake spacing in the table.

data.q: What must ATC do before the current separation method becomes insufficient?
o: Wait for the aircraft to report a loss
Establish another valid form of separation
Transfer all responsibility to the pilots
data.e: ATC establishes another valid method before the existing separation becomes insufficient.

data.q: What does Bali state about cruise climb in Indian FIRs?
o: It is compulsory in RVSM airspace
data.e: Bali states that cruise climb is not permitted in Indian FIRs.

data.q: For aircraft climbing or descending on reciprocal tracks without lateral separation, how long is vertical separation protected around estimated passing?
o: At least 10 minutes before and 10 minutes after
data.e: Vertical separation is provided for at least 10 minutes before and after the estimated passing time.

data.q: What is the normal horizontal surveillance minimum stated by Bali?
data.e: Bali states 5 NM as the normal horizontal surveillance minimum, with 3 NM only where specifically authorised.

data.q: Which category includes aircraft above 7,000 kg but below 136,000 kg maximum take-off mass?
data.e: The MEDIUM category covers aircraft above 7,000 kg but below 136,000 kg.

data.q: When may a one-minute interval be used between two departures under Bali's stated divergence case?
o: Only when vertical separation already exists
Whenever the preceding aircraft is faster
When both aircraft fly the same SID
When their tracks diverge by at least 45 degrees immediately after take-off
data.e: One minute applies when the departure tracks diverge by at least 45 degrees immediately after take-off.

data.q: What speed relationship supports Bali's two-minute same-track departure interval?
o: The following aircraft is at least 20 kt faster
The preceding aircraft is at least 40 kt faster
Both aircraft have identical filed speeds
The preceding aircraft is at least 10 kt faster
data.e: The two-minute same-track case requires the preceding aircraft to be 40 kt or more faster than the following aircraft.

data.q: For a straight-in arrival, until when may a departure take off in any direction?
o: Until 3 minutes before the arrival reaches the runway
Until the arrival crosses the final approach fix
Until 5 minutes before the arrival is estimated over the instrument runway
data.e: A departure in any direction is permitted only until 5 minutes before the straight-in arrival is estimated over the instrument runway.

data.q: Which situation can support reduced separation near an aerodrome?
o: The following crew has the preceding aircraft in sight and can maintain separation
Both aircraft are using the same runway
The controller has issued traffic information only
The crews can hear each other on frequency
data.e: One permitted case is the following crew reporting the preceding aircraft in sight and confirming that separation can be maintained.

data.q: What Bali visibility figure applies to a Category C aeroplane requesting a visual approach, before comparison with the operating minimum?
data.e: Bali states 3,200 m for a Category C aeroplane, with the higher applicable operating minimum still governing.

data.q: Up to what level may the specified own-separation-in-VMC climb or descent be cleared?
data.e: The clearance is for a specified portion at or below 3,050 m, which is 10,000 ft.

data.q: At what expected delay does Bali require an EAT to be determined?
data.e: An EAT is determined when the arriving aircraft is expected to be delayed by 10 minutes or more.

data.q: When is a revised EAT transmitted without delay under Bali's normal threshold?
o: When it differs by 5 minutes or more
data.e: The normal revision threshold is a difference of 5 minutes or more, unless a smaller agreed period applies.

data.q: What departure information is passed without delay when its status changes?
o: A visual or non-visual aid essential for take-off and climb
data.e: A change in the operational status of an aid essential for take-off and climb is passed without delay.

data.q: Which mean wind-component change is significant at the commencement of final approach according to Bali?
data.e: Bali lists 2 kt as the significant change in the mean tail-wind component.

data.q: What does an expected onward clearance time tell a held aircraft?
o: When it can expect to leave the fix where it is being held
data.e: Expected onward clearance time is the time at which the aircraft can expect to leave the fix where it is held.

data.q: Which item is essential local traffic when it may create a collision hazard?
o: Only vehicles actually on the runway
An aircraft, vehicle or person on or near the runway
Only an aircraft inside controlled airspace
data.e: Essential local traffic includes an aircraft, vehicle or person on or near the runway when it may constitute a collision hazard.

data.q: Which working position normally controls traffic on the manoeuvring area except runways?
data.e: The ground controller normally controls manoeuvring-area traffic except the runways.

data.q: During low-visibility procedures, how should vehicle and person movements on the manoeuvring area be managed?
o: They are restricted to the essential minimum and ILS sensitive areas are protected
data.e: Low-visibility procedures restrict persons and vehicles to the essential minimum and protect ILS critical and sensitive areas.

data.q: What must a pilot report with a start-up request under Bali's procedure?
o: Persons on board including crew, plus security-check completion
data.e: The start-up request includes total persons on board, including crew, and confirmation that the security check is complete.

data.q: If a taxi limit lies beyond a runway, what must the clearance contain?
o: A request to report the runway in sight
An explicit crossing clearance or instruction to hold short
data.e: A taxi clearance beyond a runway must explicitly clear the crossing or instruct the aircraft to hold short.

data.q: What distance from the runway edge does Bali state for a runway 900 m or longer, unless the marked holding position governs?
data.e: For a runway 900 m or longer, Bali states the holding position or at least 50 m from the runway edge.

data.q: What instruction follows when an obstruction threatens an aircraft already cleared to land?
data.e: The controller instructs the landing aircraft to go around when a runway obstruction threatens safety.

data.q: How is ATIS receipt normally acknowledged on first contact?
o: By reporting the current phonetic designator
By stating the observation time only
By reading back the runway condition
data.e: The pilot reports the current ATIS phonetic designator, after which ATC passes later changes or missing items.

data.q: What is the tower's first action when VFR operations are suspended?
o: Close the aerodrome to IFR traffic
data.e: The suspension procedure begins by holding all VFR departures.

data.q: Which aircraft normally has priority between an aircraft on final and one ready to depart from the same runway?
o: The departure because it is ready
The aircraft landing or in the final stages of approach
data.e: An aircraft landing or in the final stages of approach normally has priority over a departure from the same or intersecting runway.

data.q: When does Bali require aeronautical ground lights by day in India?
o: When visibility is 5,000 m or less
Only at the pilot's home aerodrome
data.e: From sunrise to sunset, Bali requires the lights when visibility in India is 5,000 m or less.

data.q: A measured runway friction coefficient of 0.27 corresponds to which assessment?
data.e: A coefficient from 0.29 to 0.26 is medium to poor and carries code 2.

data.q: To what approximate height does Bali extend the low-level wind-shear description?
data.e: Bali describes low-level wind shear from the surface to approximately 1,500 ft.

data.q: Which surveillance system can detect a reflecting aircraft without an airborne transponder?
data.e: PSR detects reflected radio energy and therefore does not require an airborne transponder.

data.q: What determines when ADS-C sends a normal surveillance report?
o: The terms and triggers in the ground-held contract
A broadcast request from every nearby aircraft
The rotation rate of a radar antenna
data.e: ADS-C reports according to the periodic, event or demand conditions defined in its ground-held contract.

data.q: How does multilateration calculate aircraft position?
o: From a single reflected radar pulse
From the code selected by the pilot alone
From a magnetic bearing reported by radio
From differences in arrival time at several receivers
data.e: MLAT calculates position from the time differences with which several receivers obtain the same transmission.

data.q: What communication condition normally supports an ATS surveillance service?
o: A listening watch on a company frequency only
Direct two-way communication with the unit providing the service
data.e: Direct two-way communication with the unit providing the surveillance service is normally required.

data.q: Under the PSR departing-aircraft method, where should identification normally be established?
o: Within 1 NM of the end of the runway used
Within 10 NM of the aerodrome boundary
data.e: The departing-aircraft method requires correlation within 1 NM of the runway end, with care to prevent confusion.

data.q: Unless another minimum is prescribed, what ICAO surveillance separation minimum does Bali state?
data.e: Bali states 5.0 NM, or 9.3 km, as the general ICAO surveillance minimum unless otherwise prescribed.

data.q: What code is selected before entry into an Indian FIR if no SSR code has been assigned?
data.e: Bali requires Mode A3 code 2000 before Indian FIR entry when no code has been assigned.

data.q: Which special code indicates radio communication failure?
data.e: Mode A code 7600 indicates radio communication failure.

data.q: What altitude-data tolerance does Bali state for RVSM airspace?
data.e: Bali uses a tolerance of plus or minus 200 ft for pressure-altitude data in RVSM airspace.

data.q: What normally happens after an in-flight transponder failure where carriage is mandatory?
o: The flight may continue to the next intended landing, subject to coordination
The aircraft must land immediately on the nearest runway
The pilot selects 0000 and continues without advising ATS
data.e: A flight with an in-flight transponder failure is normally allowed to continue to its next intended landing, subject to coordination and safety restrictions.

data.q: What should a pilot do if an ACAS RA conflicts with an ATC vertical instruction?
o: Ignore the RA because ATC always has priority
Maintain level until ATC repeats the instruction
Follow the RA and inform ATC as soon as workload permits
data.e: The pilot follows the RA even when it conflicts with an ATC instruction, then informs ATC as soon as workload permits.

data.q: What risk is addressed by a minimum safe altitude warning?
o: Unsafe proximity to terrain or obstacles
data.e: MSAW warns a controller that a tracked aircraft is at, or predicted to be at, an unsafe altitude relative to terrain or obstacles.

data.q: Where is full MOC provided in a track-guided protected area?
data.e: Full MOC applies across the primary area; in each secondary area it tapers to zero at the outer edge.

data.q: What engine condition is assumed in the design of a published instrument departure?
data.e: PANS-OPS departure procedures assume all engines are operating, so the operator develops the engine-out contingency.

data.q: What standard PDG is assumed unless another gradient is published?
data.e: The standard procedure design gradient is 3.3 percent.

data.q: At what rate does MOC increase from zero at the DER?
data.e: MOC increases at 0.8 percent of horizontal distance from the DER.

data.q: Which initial alignment defines a straight departure?
o: Within 15 degrees of runway centre line
data.e: A straight departure has an initial track within 15 degrees of runway centre-line alignment.

data.q: What height above DER elevation is normally reached before an aeroplane begins a turning departure?
data.e: An aeroplane normally flies straight until at least 120 m, 394 ft, above DER elevation.

data.q: How far from the runway beginning is an omnidirectional turn normally not initiated sooner?
data.e: The basic omnidirectional design does not initiate a turn sooner than 600 m from the runway beginning.

data.q: Where does a SID normally terminate?
o: At the first en-route fix, facility or waypoint
data.e: A SID terminates at the first fix, facility or waypoint of the en-route phase.

data.q: How does RNAV normally fly a fly-by waypoint?
o: It waits for a radio call
It ignores the waypoint in wind
It anticipates the turn to intercept the next leg
data.e: At a fly-by waypoint, RNAV anticipates the turn and intercepts the next leg smoothly.

data.q: Who develops the contingency procedure for an engine failure after V1?
data.e: The operator is responsible for the engine-failure contingency procedure after V1.

data.q: Which procedure delays acceleration to reduce noise close to the aerodrome?
data.e: NADP 1 delays acceleration and clean-up to reduce close-in noise.

data.q: Below which height should the first noise-driven action not begin?
data.e: The first noise-driven thrust or acceleration action should not begin below 800 ft above aerodrome elevation.

data.q: Which threshold IAS places an aeroplane in Category C?
data.e: Category C covers a threshold IAS from 121 to 140 kt.

data.q: Which segment normally connects the en-route phase to the IAF?
data.e: The arrival segment connects the en-route structure or STAR to the IAF.

data.q: What obstacle clearance does an MSA or TAA provide within its 25 NM area?
o: At least 600 m in every case
data.e: An MSA or TAA provides at least 300 m, 1,000 ft, obstacle clearance within 25 NM.

data.q: What is the maximum normal initial-segment intercept angle for a precision approach?
data.e: The precision initial-segment intercept angle is limited to 90 degrees.

data.q: Which point begins the final segment of a precision approach?
data.e: The FAP is where the intermediate altitude meets the precision glide path and the final segment begins.

data.q: What is the optimum final-approach descent angle with a FAF?
data.e: The optimum is 3.0 degrees, equivalent to about 5.2 percent or 318 ft per NM.

data.q: Which operational minimum is used for a non-precision approach?
o: OCA/H as the operational minimum in every case
data.e: An NPA uses MDA/H; OCA/H is the design value from which the operational minimum is derived.

data.q: What is the normal minimum missed-approach climb gradient?
data.e: The standard missed-approach construction uses a minimum climb gradient of 2.5 percent.

data.q: What should the pilot do first if visual reference is lost while circling?
o: Begin a climbing turn towards the landing runway and aerodrome
Turn directly away from the aerodrome
data.e: The circling missed approach begins with a climbing turn towards the landing runway and aerodrome before joining the published missed track.

data.q: How long is the outbound holding leg at or below 14,000 ft in still air?
data.e: At or below 14,000 ft, the standard outbound holding time is one minute.

data.q: Which entry flies 30 degrees from the reciprocal inbound track on the holding side?
data.e: The offset entry flies a track 30 degrees from the reciprocal on the holding side.

data.q: Which statement describes Mode 2 parallel approaches?
o: Approaches are independent with no adjacent radar minimum
One runway is reserved for departures
Radar separation minima are prescribed between adjacent approaches
data.e: Mode 2 is the dependent parallel-approach mode, so radar separation minima are prescribed between adjacent approaches.

data.q: Which setting makes an altimeter indicate altitude above mean sea level?
data.e: QNH makes the altimeter indicate altitude referenced to mean sea level.

data.q: What should a correctly set QFE altimeter indicate at its reference datum?
data.e: QFE is the pressure at the stated datum, so the altimeter indicates zero there.

data.q: What is QNE?
o: The expected touchdown indication with standard pressure set
data.e: QNE is the calculated altimeter indication at touchdown when standard pressure is set.

data.q: When climbing, where is the altimeter changed from QNH to standard pressure?
o: At the lowest usable flight level only
data.e: On climb, standard pressure is set when passing the transition altitude.

data.q: What is the lowest transition altitude stated by Bali for India?
data.e: Bali states that the lowest transition altitude in India is 4,000 ft.

data.q: How is the lowest usable flight level related to minimum flight altitude?
o: It is always one level below it
It corresponds to or lies immediately above it
data.e: The lowest usable flight level corresponds to, or lies immediately above, the established minimum flight altitude.

data.q: What setting is normally used en route above transition altitude?
data.e: Above transition altitude after changeover, 1013.2 hPa is used and vertical position is reported as a flight level.

data.q: What is Bali's pre-flight tolerance for an altimeter with a 0 to 30,000 ft test range?
data.e: For a test range of 0 to 30,000 ft, Bali gives a tolerance of plus or minus 60 ft.

data.q: What happens to true altitude when temperature is colder than standard at a constant indicated altitude?
data.e: In colder-than-standard air, pressure surfaces contract and true altitude is lower than indicated.

data.q: Which IFR family normally applies to magnetic tracks from 180 through 359 degrees?
data.e: Tracks from 180 through 359 degrees use the even-thousand IFR family.

data.q: Which statement about transition level is correct?
o: It is fixed for the State
It is always equal to transition altitude
It is selected by the pilot after take-off
data.e: Transition level changes with QNH so the transition layer remains protected.

data.q: If a pressure setting higher than the correct value is set, what is the main hazard?
o: The aircraft is lower than indicated
The aircraft is always higher than indicated
The flight level becomes an altitude automatically
data.e: A setting that is too high makes the altimeter over-read, so the aircraft is lower than indicated.

data.q: Which ICAO Annex contains the Standards and Recommended Practices for aeronautical information services?
data.e: Annex 15 contains the Standards and Recommended Practices for aeronautical information services.

data.q: Which product is primarily used for a permanent change to AIP content?
data.e: An AIP amendment is the controlled product for a permanent change to AIP content.

data.q: Which three principal parts form an AIP?
data.e: The AIP is divided into GEN, ENR and AD.

data.q: A temporary change will last four months. Which product normally carries it?
data.e: An AIP supplement carries a temporary change of three months or longer.

data.q: Which Indian NOTAM series does Bali associate with general and lasting information affecting aircraft operations?
data.e: Bali describes Series G as carrying general and lasting information affecting aircraft operations.

data.q: What does Item E of a NOTAM contain?
o: The operational text in standard plain language and abbreviations
data.e: Item E contains the operational text, expressed with standard language and abbreviations.

data.q: What is the interval between common AIRAC effective dates?
data.e: AIRAC common effective dates occur at intervals of 28 days.

data.q: Which special-series message reports operationally significant volcanic activity or volcanic ash?
data.e: ASHTAM reports an operationally significant change in volcanic activity, eruption or ash cloud.

data.q: What is a PIB?
o: A plain-language pre-flight summary of current NOTAM and urgent information
A permanent amendment to the AIP
data.e: A PIB is a plain-language pre-flight summary of current NOTAM and other urgent information.

data.q: What is the main purpose of WGS 84 in aeronautical information?
o: To provide one common geodetic datum for published coordinates
data.e: WGS 84 provides a common geodetic datum for coordinates used by charts, databases and navigation systems.

data.q: When should a trigger NOTAM become effective?
o: When the next checklist is printed
On the same effective date as the AIRAC amendment or supplement
data.e: A trigger NOTAM comes into force on the same effective date as the AIRAC amendment or supplement it announces.

data.q: What should a crew report through the post-flight information process?
o: Observed defects in navigation facilities and operational hazards
data.e: Post-flight information includes observed defects in navigation facilities and hazards such as birds or wildlife near an aerodrome.

data.q: Which area includes the manoeuvring area and aprons?
data.e: The movement area includes the manoeuvring area, aprons and relevant aircraft-maintenance movement areas.

data.q: What determines aerodrome reference-code element 2?
o: Wingspan and outer main gear wheel span
data.e: Element 2 is the letter determined from wingspan and outer main gear wheel span.

data.q: What is the minimum RESA length stated in the lesson?
data.e: The RESA extends at least 90 m from the end of the runway strip.

data.q: Which relationship normally defines ASDA?
data.e: ASDA normally equals TORA plus any available stopway.

data.q: At a runway and taxiway intersection, which markings continue?
data.e: Runway markings continue through a runway and taxiway intersection, while taxiway markings are interrupted.

data.q: How is a permanently displaced threshold shown?
o: By white arrows leading to a transverse white threshold stripe
By a red stop bar painted on the runway
data.e: White arrows lead to the transverse white stripe that marks a displaced threshold.

data.q: How far from the threshold does an aiming-point marking begin when LDA is 2,400 m or more?
data.e: For an LDA of 2,400 m or more, the aiming-point marking starts 400 m from the threshold.

data.q: Which description identifies Pattern A?
o: Two solid and two broken yellow lines
A yellow circle with an arrow
data.e: Pattern A consists of two solid and two broken yellow lines across the taxiway.

data.q: What is the diameter of a VOR aerodrome-checkpoint circle?
data.e: The VOR aerodrome-checkpoint circle is 6 m in diameter.

data.q: Which colour combination identifies a mandatory instruction sign?
data.e: A mandatory instruction sign uses a white inscription on a red background.

data.q: What does a yellow inscription on a black sign identify?
data.e: A yellow inscription on black is a location sign showing the current taxiway, runway or pavement.

data.q: What does a runway-vacated sign depict?
data.e: A runway-vacated sign depicts the Pattern A holding-position symbol.

data.q: What display identifies a land-aerodrome identification beacon?
data.e: A land-aerodrome identification beacon flashes green characters in International Morse Code.

data.q: What distinguishes the inner 300 m of a precision category II or III approach-light system?
o: White centre-line barrettes with red side-row barrettes
data.e: The inner 300 m is strengthened by white centre-line barrettes and red side-row barrettes.

data.q: Which PAPI display means the aircraft is on the nominal approach slope?
data.e: Two white and two red is the standard PAPI on-slope indication.

data.q: What colour are runway centre-line lights for the final 300 m?
data.e: Runway centre-line lights are red throughout the final 300 m.

data.q: What does an illuminated stop bar require?
o: Follow the green centre line without stopping
Stop and do not cross while it remains illuminated
data.e: An illuminated red stop bar is a stop instruction and must not be crossed.

data.q: Which obstacle surface protects the initial take-off climb?
data.e: The take-off climb surface is the inclined, widening plane beyond the runway or clearway end.

data.q: How are high-intensity obstacle lights displayed?
data.e: High-intensity obstacle lights are flashing white and may be used by day as well as night.

data.q: Which overall-length band defines RFF category 8?
data.e: Category 8 covers overall lengths from 49 m up to, but not including, 61 m.

data.q: What can happen when highest-category movements are fewer than 700 in the busiest consecutive three months?
o: Protection may be one category lower
Dry chemical agent is no longer required
data.e: Subject to the stated condition, the protection provided may be one category below the determined category.

data.q: Which item belongs in a disabled-aircraft removal plan?
o: A coordinator and available lifting or towing resources
data.e: The removal plan identifies a coordinator, equipment, routes, communications and recovery information.

data.q: What is a principal purpose of apron management?
o: Prevent collisions and coordinate apron movement
data.e: Apron management regulates movement to prevent collisions and coordinates apron entry, exit and vehicle activity.

data.q: What is a primary control for wildlife hazard?
o: Permit food waste near the runway
Manage habitat and attractants, then monitor and disperse wildlife
data.e: Wildlife risk is reduced through habitat and attractant control, surveillance, dispersal and reporting.

data.q: What does an AOC or permit authorise?
data.e: An AOC or permit authorises the operator to conduct specified commercial air transport operations.

data.q: Which item belongs in the operational-manual group carried on board?
data.e: The Minimum Equipment List is one of the operational documents carried for the flight.

data.q: Who makes the final decision about admitting a permitted person to the flight deck?
data.e: The commander retains the final responsibility for admission to the flight deck.

data.q: What additive produces Restricted AOM from Normal AOM in Bali?
data.e: Restricted AOM adds 100 ft to DA/H or MDA/H and 400 m to visibility or RVR.

data.q: What vertical separation is applied in RVSM airspace from FL 290 to FL 410 inclusive?
data.e: RVSM applies 1,000 ft vertical separation between FL 290 and FL 410 inclusive.

data.q: Which statement correctly compares MEL and MMEL?
o: The MMEL is written for one individual flight
The operator MEL cannot be less restrictive than the MMEL
data.e: An operator's approved MEL is derived from and cannot be less restrictive than the aircraft-type MMEL.

data.q: Below which compartment pressure must oxygen cover crew and passengers for any period?
data.e: For any period below 620 hPa, oxygen must be available for crew and passengers.

data.q: What is turbine-aeroplane final reserve fuel?
o: 45 minutes at holding speed at sea level
30 minutes at holding speed 1,500 ft above the aerodrome
Five per cent of taxi fuel
data.e: For a turbine aeroplane, final reserve is 30 minutes at holding speed 1,500 ft above aerodrome elevation in standard conditions.

data.q: Which aeronautical emergency frequency must the communication equipment support?
data.e: The aircraft radio equipment must support aeronautical emergency frequency 121.5 MHz.

data.q: How long must FDTL duty and rest records be retained?
data.e: Bali states that records of duties and rest periods are kept for 18 months.

data.q: What is the maximum two-pilot FDP for four landings in Bali's table?
data.e: For four landings, the table permits 8 hours flight time and a maximum FDP of 12 hours.

data.q: Which term means block time from first movement for take-off until final rest after flight?
data.e: Flight time is block-to-block time from first movement for take-off until final rest after landing.

data.q: What is the relationship between an operator's MEL and the approved MMEL?
o: The MEL replaces all Flight Manual limits
The MMEL applies only to one flight
The MEL cannot be less restrictive than the MMEL
data.e: The operator's approved MEL is tailored from, and cannot be less restrictive than, the approved MMEL.

data.q: When does holdover time begin?
o: At the start of the final de-icing or anti-icing application
At the end of the first inspection
data.e: Holdover time begins at the start of the final de-icing or anti-icing application.

data.q: What should a pilot do first when exposed to a strong laser beam on approach?
o: Descend below the beam without informing ATC
Stare at the source to identify it
Look away and maintain control using instruments
data.e: The pilot should look away from the beam, maintain control on instruments and transfer control if needed.

data.q: Which agent principle is correct for an energised class C electrical fire?
o: Add fuel to cool the wiring
data.e: A class C electrical fire requires an approved nonconducting agent such as halon or carbon dioxide.

data.q: What is the immediate crew priority after explosive decompression at high altitude?
o: Ask ATC for a route shortcut
Put on oxygen masks and control the aircraft
data.e: The crew first put on oxygen masks and control the aircraft before communication and assessment.

data.q: Which sequence describes a microburst encounter on approach?
o: Tailwind gain followed by calm air
data.e: A microburst typically gives a headwind gain, then a downdraft, followed by a dangerous tailwind loss.

data.q: When are wingtip vortices strongest?
o: When the generating aircraft is heavy, clean and slow
When it is light, dirty and fast
data.e: Wake vortices are strongest when the generating aircraft is heavy, clean and slow.

data.q: What surveillance wake minimum applies to an A380 followed by a Light aircraft in Bali's table?
data.e: Bali's surveillance table gives 8 NM for an A380 followed by a Light aircraft.

data.q: What vertical position is required for traffic behind a fuel-jettisoning aircraft within the protected trail area?
o: At least 1,000 ft above or 3,000 ft below
At least 3,000 ft above or 1,000 ft below
data.e: Traffic behind within the protected distance remains at least 1,000 ft above or 3,000 ft below.

data.q: What mainly characterises dynamic hydroplaning?
o: The tyre gains extra friction from water
Water pressure lifts the tyre from the pavement
The wheel brakes become more effective
data.e: In dynamic hydroplaning, water pressure lifts the tyre from the pavement and greatly reduces braking and directional control.

data.q: Which dangerous-goods class contains corrosives?
data.e: Class 8 is the dangerous-goods class for corrosive substances.

data.q: Which organisation issues volcanic ash advisory information for its assigned area?
data.e: A Volcanic Ash Advisory Centre analyses the hazard and issues volcanic ash advisory information.

data.q: Which unit coordinates search and rescue operations throughout one SAR region?
data.e: The Rescue Coordination Centre organises SAR service and coordinates operations throughout its SAR region.

data.q: Which organisation coordinates maritime SAR policy in Bali's Indian framework?
o: The National Maritime Search and Rescue Board
data.e: The National Maritime Search and Rescue Board coordinates maritime SAR policy under the Indian Coast Guard leadership described by Bali.

data.q: What does INCERFA mean?
o: The aircraft has requested medical assistance
Uncertainty exists about the safety of an aircraft and its occupants
data.e: INCERFA is the uncertainty phase, in which uncertainty exists about aircraft and occupant safety.

data.q: Which statement best describes DETRESFA action by an RCC?
o: Wait for a scheduled report before acting
Initiate the coordinated search and rescue plan without delay
Transfer all responsibility to the operator
data.e: During DETRESFA the RCC initiates the coordinated search and rescue plan without delay.

data.q: Who normally takes initial on-scene charge when the first arriving aircraft is not a dedicated SAR aircraft?
o: The pilot of the first aircraft
data.e: The pilot of the first aircraft takes temporary on-scene charge until agreed transfer or arrival of a dedicated SAR aircraft.

data.q: Which search pattern is best suited to a precisely known datum and compact area?
data.e: An expanding-square search begins near an accurate datum and expands systematically through a compact area.

data.q: How does an aircraft direct a surface craft toward survivors when radio communication is unavailable?
o: Circle it, cross close ahead while attracting attention, then fly the required direction
Cross its wake close astern and depart
Flash the landing lights once and climb
data.e: The directing sequence is to circle, cross close ahead while attracting attention, and then head toward the distress site.

data.q: What does the survivor ground symbol X mean?
data.e: The survivor symbol X means require medical assistance.

data.q: What is the primary role of the 406 MHz component of an ELT?
o: Satellite distress alerting with coded identity
data.e: The 406 MHz ELT transmission provides coded satellite distress alerting through COSPAS-SARSAT.

data.q: What is the defining assessment in ALERFA?
o: Apprehension exists about aircraft and occupant safety
data.e: ALERFA is the alert phase, when apprehension exists about the safety of the aircraft and occupants.

data.q: How does an aircraft acknowledge a ground signal at night?
o: By flashing landing lights twice, or navigation lights twice if needed
data.e: At night the aircraft flashes its landing lights twice or, if unavailable, switches navigation lights on and off twice.

data.q: Which streamer colour identifies food and water in droppable SAR supplies?
data.e: Blue streamers identify packages containing food and water.

data.q: What is the sole objective of an Annex 13 safety investigation?
o: To prevent future accidents and incidents
data.e: The sole objective is prevention of future accidents and incidents, not apportionment of blame or liability.

data.q: When does an injury count as fatal under Bali's national accident definition?
o: When it causes death within 30 days of the accident
data.e: Bali treats an accident injury as fatal when death occurs within 30 days of the accident date.

data.q: Which event is a typical serious incident?
o: A near collision requiring an avoidance manoeuvre
data.e: A near collision requiring avoidance is a typical serious incident because an accident nearly occurred.

data.q: What is the correct timing principle for notifying AAIB?
o: Wait until every fact is confirmed
Notify only after the final report
Notify promptly by the quickest means and within Bali's 24-hour limit
Notify at the next licence renewal
data.e: Known facts are notified promptly by the quickest means, with Bali's outer limit of 24 hours after awareness.

data.q: Which State normally institutes an investigation for an occurrence in its territory?
data.e: The State of Occurrence normally institutes and conducts the territorial investigation.

data.q: Who normally investigates an accident in India under the 2017 Rules?
data.e: AAIB investigates accidents under the Aircraft (Investigation of Accidents and Incidents) Rules, 2017.

data.q: What takes priority over preserving an untouched wreckage site?
o: Rescue of people and removal of immediate danger
data.e: Lifesaving rescue and removal of immediate danger take priority, with necessary disturbance documented.

data.q: What is ADREP?
o: ICAO's Accident and Incident Data Reporting system
data.e: ADREP is ICAO's standardised Accident and Incident Data Reporting system.

data.q: Which statement describes just culture?
o: Proportionate honest actions are protected while wilful misconduct remains accountable
No one can ever be disciplined
data.e: Just culture protects proportionate honest actions while retaining accountability for wilful misconduct and similarly unacceptable behaviour.

data.q: Who may also notify AAIB besides the pilot or operator?
o: The aerodrome operator, ATS unit and DGCA where applicable
data.e: The aerodrome operator, ATS unit concerned and DGCA where applicable also submit notification to AAIB.

data.q: Which Indian body normally investigates other incidents not assigned to AAIB by the serious-incident criteria?
data.e: DGCA normally investigates incidents and serious incidents not assigned to AAIB, unless AAIB takes over.

data.q: What is the purpose of a safety recommendation?
o: To address a safety deficiency and prevent recurrence
data.e: A safety recommendation proposes preventive action to address an identified safety deficiency.

data.q: What is the main purpose of Annex 9 facilitation?
o: To expedite international air transport while maintaining necessary controls
To replace customs with airline staff
data.e: Annex 9 expedites aircraft, people and goods while preserving necessary customs, immigration, health, security and law-enforcement controls.

data.q: What happens when an aircraft-clearance document has been accepted electronically?
o: The same document should not also be demanded on paper
It may be ignored by authorities
It must always be sent twice
data.e: Once authorities accept the required electronic document, they should not demand the identical document again on paper.

data.q: Who may sign the General Declaration?
o: The pilot-in-command or an authorised agent
data.e: The General Declaration may be signed by the pilot-in-command or an authorised agent.

data.q: What is the purpose of a direct transit area?
o: To replace the runway holding point
To let transit passengers remain under supervision without applying for entry
data.e: A direct transit area lets passengers remain under authority supervision during transfer without applying to enter the State.

data.q: How is unaccompanied baggage normally cleared?
o: Under cargo procedures with a simplified process
data.e: Unaccompanied baggage follows cargo clearance procedures but may use a simplified process.

data.q: Which principle applies to assistance for a passenger with a disability?
o: The journey chain should be coordinated with dignity and accessible communication
Mobility aids are always left behind
data.e: Facilitation coordinates accessible assistance through the journey while respecting dignity, autonomy and safety.

data.q: Which statement correctly distinguishes an inadmissible person from a deportee?
o: An inadmissible person must be airline crew
A deportee is always a transit passenger
An inadmissible person is refused entry, while a deportee is formally ordered to leave after admission or presence
data.e: Inadmissibility is refusal of entry; deportation is formal removal of a person already admitted or present.

data.q: What is disinsection intended to control?
o: Insects capable of carrying disease or pests
data.e: Disinsection uses an approved treatment to control insects that can carry disease or agricultural pests.

data.q: Which channel is used in India by an arriving passenger with no dutiable goods?
data.e: An arriving passenger with no dutiable goods uses the Green Channel and remains responsible for an accurate declaration.

data.q: Which three standard aircraft documents are central to the chapter?
o: General Declaration, Passenger Manifest and Cargo Manifest
Load sheet, fuel sheet and journey log
Weather chart, flight plan and tech log
data.e: The standard facilitation documents are the General Declaration, Passenger Manifest and Cargo Manifest.

data.q: Who normally arranges removal after a border authority refuses a passenger admission?
o: The operator under the State's removal order
data.e: After the State refuses admission and issues the removal direction, the operator normally arranges carriage to the specified admissible point.

data.q: What must happen before an international flight leaves India according to Bali's national provision?
o: The cargo manifest must be destroyed
All passengers must use the Red Channel
Immigration and customs clearance must be obtained on the General Declaration
data.e: Bali states that immigration and customs authorities must clear the flight on the General Declaration before departure from India.

data.q: What is the primary objective of Annex 17 security measures?
o: Safety of passengers, crew, ground personnel and the public
data.e: The safety of passengers, crew, ground personnel and the public is the primary Annex 17 objective.

data.q: Which body is India’s specialist civil aviation security regulator and oversight authority?
data.e: The Bureau of Civil Aviation Security, BCAS, sets standards and oversees civil aviation security in India.

data.q: What does a security quality-control test establish?
o: Whether an aircraft can meet take-off performance
Whether a control detects or prevents a simulated threat
Whether a passenger has a visa
data.e: A security test challenges a control under managed conditions to see whether it detects or prevents a simulated threat.

data.q: What distinguishes a security restricted area from a general landside area?
o: It is a priority risk area with additional access and security controls
It is always outside the airport fence
It is open to every ticket holder
data.e: A security restricted area is a priority risk area where additional access and security controls apply.

data.q: What is required if screened passengers mix with unscreened persons after the screening point?
o: No action if the flight is ready
The affected passengers and cabin baggage must be screened again
data.e: Mixing breaks the sterile flow, so affected passengers and their cabin baggage must be screened again before boarding.

data.q: When can screened cargo continue to be treated as secure?
o: Only when it travels with a passenger
Even after an unexplained access breach
Only while it remains protected from unauthorised interference
data.e: Screened cargo retains secure status only while it remains protected from unauthorised interference.

data.q: Which statement correctly compares an aircraft security check and search?
o: A search is the more thorough interior and exterior inspection
A check is always more extensive
data.e: An aircraft security search is the more thorough inspection of interior, exterior and defined concealed areas.

data.q: Who must receive operationally necessary information about an authorised armed person aboard?
data.e: The pilot-in-command must receive the information needed to manage authorised armed carriage safely.

data.q: What is the normal action when an unlawfully seized aircraft lands in a State?
o: Move all passengers to another flight without coordination
Require immediate departure in every case
Release it whenever the operator asks
Retain it on the ground unless protection of human life requires departure
data.e: The State normally retains the aircraft on the ground, with an exception when the overriding duty to protect human life requires departure.

data.q: What is the AVSEC Panel’s central role?
o: Advising ICAO on security standards, threats and Annex 17 amendments
data.e: The AVSEC Panel advises ICAO on emerging threats, vulnerabilities, security standards and proposed Annex 17 amendments.

data.q: Which national document coordinates security responsibilities and required controls across India?
o: The National Civil Aviation Security Programme
data.e: The National Civil Aviation Security Programme coordinates national aviation security responsibilities, standards and controls.

data.q: Which recipients are explicitly part of the landing notification chain after an act of unlawful interference?
o: The States of Registry and Operator, affected-national States and ICAO
Only the next air traffic control unit
data.e: The notification chain includes the States of Registry and Operator, relevant States connected to affected citizens and ICAO.
